text: Given a valid X-Digitalocean-Token and DigitalOcean returns 2 namespaces, When digitalocean_list_namespaces is called, Then both namespaces are returned as-is.
Given DigitalOcean returns zero namespaces, When digitalocean_list_namespaces is called, Then the tool returns an empty array, not an error.
Given label and region, When digitalocean_create_namespace is called, Then the body is POSTed and the created namespace is returned.
Given region is omitted, When digitalocean_create_namespace is called, Then the tool returns invalid_argument without calling DigitalOcean.
Given an existing namespace_id, When digitalocean_get_namespace is called, Then its details are returned.
Given a namespace_id DigitalOcean 404s on, When digitalocean_get_namespace is called, Then the tool returns a structured not_found, not a raw 404 or 500.
Given an existing namespace_id, When digitalocean_delete_namespace is called, Then the matching DELETE is issued and success is confirmed.
Given no namespace_id is supplied, When digitalocean_delete_namespace is called, Then the tool rejects the call before any upstream request (invalid_argument).
Given an existing namespace_id with 2 triggers, When digitalocean_list_triggers is called, Then both triggers are returned.
Given a namespace with zero triggers, When digitalocean_list_triggers is called, Then the tool returns an empty array, not an error.
Given name, function, type, is_enabled, scheduled_details, When digitalocean_create_trigger is called, Then the full body is posted and the created trigger returned.
Given a required field (e.g. type) is missing, When digitalocean_create_trigger is called, Then the tool returns invalid_argument without calling DigitalOcean.
Given an existing trigger_name, When digitalocean_get_trigger is called, Then its details are returned.
Given a trigger_name DigitalOcean 404s on, When digitalocean_get_trigger is called, Then the tool returns a structured not_found.
Given one or more updatable fields, When digitalocean_update_trigger is called, Then only those fields are sent via PUT and the updated trigger is returned.
Given an existing trigger, When digitalocean_delete_trigger is called, Then it is deleted and confirmed.
Given no trigger_name is supplied, When digitalocean_delete_trigger is called, Then the tool rejects the call before any upstream request.
Given an existing namespace_id with 2 access keys, When digitalocean_list_access_keys is called, Then both keys are returned, including an empty array when there are none.
Given a key configuration, When digitalocean_create_access_key is called, Then the key is created, its details (including the one-time value) are returned, and the value never appears in our logs.
Given an existing key_id, When digitalocean_update_access_key is called, Then the update is applied and the updated key returned.
Given an existing key_id, When digitalocean_delete_access_key is called, Then it is deleted and confirmed.
Given no key_id is supplied, When digitalocean_delete_access_key is called, Then the tool rejects the call before any upstream request.
Given a request with no X-Digitalocean-Token header, When any tool is called, Then the response is 401 and lists the required header name, never 500.
Given DigitalOcean returns 429 once then 200, When a tool is called, Then the client retries and the eventual success is returned to the caller.
Given DigitalOcean returns 503 for every attempt, When a tool is called, Then after bounded retries the tool returns a structured upstream_error within the time budget, never an unhandled exception.

Given two sequential requests carry two different tokens (tenant A, tenant B) against two different mocked upstream responses, When each calls digitalocean_list_namespaces, Then tenant A never receives tenant B's data and the credential contextvar is reset between requests. (multi-tenant/credential-isolation anchor, OWASP API-security adjacent)
Given DigitalOcean is unreachable (mocked timeout/connection error), When GET /health is called with no credential header, Then it still returns 200 {"status":"ok"}.
Given the generated tools/list, When inspected, Then every list_*/get_* tool has readOnlyHint true and every delete_* tool has destructiveHint true.

Given a real DigitalOcean Personal Access Token, When each of the 13 tools is exercised end-to-end against a disposable test namespace (create namespace; create/list/get/update/delete trigger; create/list/update/delete access key; delete namespace), Then every call succeeds against the live API and the namespace is left cleaned up.
steps: Obtain a real DigitalOcean Personal Access Token with Functions read/write scope
Call digitalocean_create_namespace with a disposable label/region
Call digitalocean_list_namespaces and digitalocean_get_namespace and confirm the new namespace appears
Call digitalocean_create_trigger, digitalocean_list_triggers, digitalocean_get_trigger, digitalocean_update_trigger, digitalocean_delete_trigger in sequence
Call digitalocean_create_access_key, digitalocean_list_access_keys, digitalocean_update_access_key, digitalocean_delete_access_key in sequence
Confirm no disposable resources remain on the account
expect: All 13 calls return 2xx-equivalent tool results matching the documented response shapes; the account has no leftover test namespace/trigger/key afterward
evidence: needs a real vendor account — not available at design/dev time; not a blocker per SOP "no test account" rule
